messages:
maria_gupta: quick follow-up on the retry budget RFC — thinking about how we handle streaming requests when tenants hit retry pressure. want to avoid global hedging that spikes tokens and double-bills.

alex_cheng: +1 we opened this in the RFC but didn't land a concrete mechanism for streaming fragments.

sam_lee: my read: we need a per-tenant sliding retry window + a scoring function that prefers cheap fallbacks (quantized model / shorter seq) before hedging.

maria_gupta: exactly. proposal: attach a light-weight Retry-Score to requests and stream fragments. header: X-Redwood-Retry-Score: <0..1>. score increases on failures / age.

jin_ops: curious how score interacts with batching. if we increase score mid-stream, do we reshuffle into high-priority lanes? expensive.

alex_cheng: we shouldn't re-batch mid-stream. instead: allow the origin node (edge) to start a parallel fallback only for future fragments, not already-streamed tokens. no duplicate tokens for tokens already emitted.

sam_lee: UX: streaming apps expect smooth partial output. fallback should be used only when progress stalls or SLA window exceeded. propose state machine: ACTIVE -> STALLED -> FALLBACK_PENDING -> FALLBACK_ACTIVE.

maria_gupta: agree. add a tenantRetryBudget counter updated atomically at ingress; FALLBACK_PENDING requires budget check. if budget exhausted, route to degraded mode (shorter model or cached prefix).

jin_ops: implementation nit: keep budget updates cheap. use a leaky-bucket approximation with occasional strong-consistency updates to control charges. local counters with periodic reconciliation.

alex_cheng: billing angle: we need checkpointed billing so customers are only billed for tokens actually emitted by whichever backend wins. i.e., if fallback succeeded, only count tokens from fallback path after its activation.

sam_lee: +1. Also: telemetry — emit events: retry_decision={reason, score, budget_before, budget_after, fallback_variant}. helps diagnose noisy tenants.

maria_gupta: pseudo header example for the edge to send downstream when starting fallback (so upstream model can garbage collect KV slots):

```
X-Redwood-Retry-Score: 0.82
X-Redwood-Fallback-Start: 1785556680
X-Redwood-Fallback-Variant: small-quant
```

alex_cheng: good. also add X-Redwood-Checkpoint-Tokens to indicate last-confirmed-output-offset so we don't double-charge or re-emit from older state.

jin_ops: backpressure: if upstream is overloaded, edge should gracefully back off new fragment dispatch and optionally emit progress-hint trailers to client. progress-hint could be a quick partial cached response.

sam_lee: question: how do we score side-effects? hedging could cause duplicate external effects. need idempotency tokens on the request envelope and a hedging-safe flag.

maria_gupta: agreed — require header Hedging-Safe: true for any automatic hedging. otherwise, only fallback to models that we guarantee no side-effects or use single-path fallback.

alex_cheng: actionable checklist: 1) spec headers & state transitions, 2) implement tenant leaky-bucket counter with reconciliation, 3) checkpointed billing hooks, 4) telemetry events, 5) integration test for mid-stream fallback (no double-emit).

jin_ops: I'll own 2 and 3. will prototype local counter with periodic reconciliation and provide load test results.

sam_lee: I'll do 4 and 5 — add tests that simulate stall -> fallback and verify token accounting + idempotency.

maria_gupta: I'll write the headers/state RFC follow-up doc and sync with product on acceptable degraded variants. ping me if you want to pair on examples.
